title: MCP Security II — OAuth 2.1, Resource Indicators, Incremental Scopes

questions.question: What does the authorization server verify before exchanging an OAuth code?
options: That the redirect URI is localhost
That the requested scope is empty
questions.explanation: exchange pops the code and checks both its resource indicator and the SHA-256 PKCE challenge before issuing a token.

questions.question: What response follows a notes create call when the token lacks notes:write?
options: 404 because create is not a tool
questions.explanation: The resource server distinguishes authentication from authorization: a valid token missing notes:write receives 403 and a WWW-Authenticate insufficient_scope challenge.

questions.question: What happens when a notes token is sent to another resource server?
options: It is upgraded to all scopes
It succeeds because scopes are global
It is treated as an unauthenticated notification
questions.explanation: Resource indicators bind the token to NOTES_SERVER, so a different audience fails authentication with an audience mismatch.

questions.question: How does call_with_step_up obtain permission for a missing write scope?
options: It retries the same token until the scope changes
It sends the secret verifier to the tool
It downgrades the operation to a read
questions.explanation: The client performs incremental authorization: it extracts the required scope, obtains a token containing existing plus required scopes, then retries.

questions.question: What lifetime does the issued access token use in the fake authorization server?
questions.explanation: Authorization codes expire in 600 seconds, while the issued Token records an access-token expiry of 3600 seconds.

questions.question: What error does register_client return when redirect_uris is missing?
questions.explanation: Dynamic client registration requires redirect_uris; the implementation rejects a missing list with HTTP 400 and invalid_redirect_uri.
